articles.title: Drag Chute
articles.summary: A flat matte grey surface, no shine at all, like primer or unpolished cast metal with a faint even grain. Your own colour, plainly, with a soft satin-metallic glow instead of mirror gloss; nothing else to see.
articles.what: Up close: No visible pattern: the paint is a flat even colour. Only the shine is set, uniformly: a slight metallic lift (metal 60) with a soft roughness (90) under a full clearcoat. The stretched spec strip shows only tiny blotchy variation, invisible at 1:1. From a distance: Your own colour, plainly, with a soft satin-metallic glow instead of mirror gloss; nothing else to see. Measured spec (average): metal 60, roughness 90, coat 16. Shine: satin. Metal: low. It takes the colour you give the zone.
when: Fits: dirt late model, truck / off-road, stock car.
how: This finish is not listed in the Base Material picker, so you cannot pick it there.
Open the AI copilot (the ✦ AI button, bottom right) and ask for it by name, for example "put Drag Chute on the hood".
Pick your colour with BASE COLOR.
Render and judge it on the car, not on the swatch.
tips: Whole body: it is a uniform base
Best as the ground under stripes, numbers and sponsor art
Numbers read perfectly: nothing competes with them.
Any pattern or graphic: the surface is blank, everything shows through
Pairs well with: black, olive, orange accent, white.
Not listed in the picker: ask the AI copilot for it by name.
pitfalls: Not matte primer: the clearcoat is full and there is a soft satin sheen
Not a texture: it is a plain flat finish with no pattern
Avoid: looks unfinished next to gloss, dark numbers need contrast.
articles.spec_character: Average spec: metal 60 (low metal, like carbon or subtle flake), roughness 90 (satin gloss), clearcoat 16 (maximum clearcoat). The spec is almost perfectly flat, one smooth material.
articles.intent_note: Full-finish shelf: the finish carries both its own paint look and its own shine.
articles.paint_advice: Gloss shows the paint colour as it is, so any colour works; pick the colour for contrast with the neighbouring zones, not for the finish. Avoid: looks unfinished next to gloss, dark numbers need contrast.

combos.why: Patterns that suit it: any pattern or graphic: the surface is blank, everything shows through; stripes, camo, flames, graphics: ground for livery work
Patterns to avoid: none; keep fine grain light if you want the satin to look smooth
Spec overlays that work: any texture spec pattern: carbon, grain, micro-flake; gloss band or clear panel: breaks up the uniform sheen
Judge the paint and the shine together: the same spec looks different under different colours.
